title: Reed's Conjecture (Conjecture 1.3)
statement_text: If $G$ is a graph of maximum degree at most $\Delta$ with no clique of size greater than $\omega$, then $\chi(G) \leq \left\lceil \frac{1}{2}(\Delta + 1 + \omega) \right\rceil$.
context_text: Reed's Conjecture, also called Reed's $\omega$, $\Delta$, $\chi$ Conjecture, proposes that the chromatic number is bounded by the average of the trivial greedy upper bound $\Delta+1$ and the clique number $\omega$. Reed proved a partial result (Theorem 1.4) showing $\chi(G) \leq \lceil (1-\varepsilon)(\Delta+1) + \varepsilon\omega \rceil$ for some $\varepsilon > 0$; subsequent work improved $\varepsilon$ to $1/26$ and $1/13$ for large $\Delta$.
paper_contribution: The paper's Theorem 1.6 implies Conjecture 1.3 when $\omega = o\!\left(\frac{\ln\Delta}{\ln\ln\Delta}\right)$, establishing a linear improvement on the greedy bound in this regime and extending the known family of graphs for which the conjecture holds.
paper_title: Bounding $χ$ by a fraction of $Δ$ for graphs without large cliques

title: Question 1.5
statement_text: Does there exist a function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that, for every $c > 1$ and every graph $G$ of maximum degree at most $\Delta$ with no clique of size greater than $\Delta^{1/f(c)}$, we have $\chi_\ell(G) \leq \Delta/c$?
context_text: A list-assignment $L$ gives each vertex $v$ a set $L(v)$ of available colours; $G$ is $k$-choosable if it has a proper colouring with $\phi(v)\in L(v)$ for every $v$ whenever all $|L(v)|\ge k$, and the list-chromatic number $\chi_\ell(G)$ is the least such $k$ (so $\chi\le\chi_\ell$). Molloy proved $\chi_\ell(G)\le(1+o(1))\Delta/\ln\Delta$ for triangle-free graphs of maximum degree $\Delta$, and $\chi_\ell(G)\le200\,\omega\frac{\Delta\ln\ln\Delta}{\ln\Delta}$ when there is no clique of size greater than $\omega$, which implies Reed's bound $\chi\le\lceil\frac12(\Delta+1+\omega)\rceil$ when $\omega=o(\ln\Delta/\ln\ln\Delta)$. The question asks whether a bound much stronger than Reed's holds already when $\omega$ is a small power of $\Delta$; Spencer's Ramsey construction (graphs on $n$ vertices with independence number $2$ and cliques of size at most $n^{1/2+o(1)}$) shows that nothing better than about $\Delta/2$ can hold when $\omega=\Omega(\Delta^{1/2})$. The paper answers the question affirmatively: the authors prove $\chi_\ell(G)=O\left(\Delta\sqrt{\ln\omega/\ln\Delta}\right)$, so that $f(c)=(72c)^2$ suffices for $\Delta$ large enough (in fact a local version for correspondence colouring). Determining the best possible $f$ is left open; Spencer's lower bounds on Ramsey numbers give $f(c)\ge c/2+1$ for integer $c$, and in particular $f(2)\ge2$.
notes: The paper answers Question 1.5 in the affirmative via Theorem 1.6, with $f(c) = (72c)^2$ sufficing for large enough $\Delta$.
paper_title: Bounding $χ$ by a fraction of $Δ$ for graphs without large cliques

title: List-chromatic analogue of Reed's Conjecture
statement_text: Reed's conjecture may also be true for the list-chromatic number, i.e., $\chi_\ell(G)\leq\left\lceil\frac{1}{2}(\Delta+1+\omega)\right\rceil$ for every graph $G$ of maximum degree at most $\Delta$ with no clique of size greater than $\omega$.
context_text: A list-assignment $L$ gives each vertex $v$ a set $L(v)$ of available colours; $G$ is $k$-choosable if it has a proper colouring with $\phi(v)\in L(v)$ for every $v$ whenever all $|L(v)|\ge k$, and the list-chromatic number $\chi_\ell(G)$ is the least such $k$ (so $\chi\le\chi_\ell$). Reed's $\omega,\Delta,\chi$ conjecture asserts that every graph of maximum degree at most $\Delta$ with no clique of size greater than $\omega$ satisfies $\chi(G)\le\lceil\frac12(\Delta+1+\omega)\rceil$. Reed proved that there is $\varepsilon>0$ with $\chi(G)\le\lceil(1-\varepsilon)(\Delta+1)+\varepsilon\omega\rceil$ (the conjecture is the case $\varepsilon=\frac12$); Bonamy, Perrett and Postle obtained $\varepsilon=\frac1{26}$ for large $\Delta$, and Delcourt and Postle proved the list-colouring version of Reed's theorem with $\varepsilon=\frac1{13}$ for large $\Delta$. No value $\varepsilon>\frac12$ works (Spencer's Ramsey graphs, or blowups of $C_5$, which also show that the rounding is necessary). Molloy's bound $\chi_\ell(G)\le200\,\omega\frac{\Delta\ln\ln\Delta}{\ln\Delta}$ implies the list version when $\omega=o(\ln\Delta/\ln\ln\Delta)$. The authors only remark that the list version is possible.
notes: Stated informally in the introduction: 'It is possible that Conjecture 1.3 is also true for the list-chromatic number.'
paper_title: Bounding $χ$ by a fraction of $Δ$ for graphs without large cliques
